_file: W1 caregiver exchange collection template (M1 style reference)
_supplied_by: agent (per standing rule: the agent supplies the JSON template; the content comes from real caregivers only)
_how_to_fill: 1. Send this file (or copy its structure) to one caregiver or family member.
2. Ask for 6-8 exchanges to start, covering all 4 scenes below. Full set for M1 is 15-20.
3. Tell them: write or say what you would REALLY say — not what sounds correct, not advice, not what a professional would say. Recording them speaking and transcribing works well.
4. The owner (Rohan role) reviews every entry for safety before it is used: no invented facts, no false reassurance ('he's on his way' about someone deceased), no diagnosis language, no dosing.
5. Only entries with placeholder=false AND owner_approved=true may ever be considered for the prompt. Everything else is plumbing.
_scenes: missing_priya    — Asha misses her daughter (Memory Box moment)
vikram_mention   — Asha asks for her late husband (avoid-topic / gentle redirect)
repetition       — Asha asks the same question for the 3rd+ time
anxious_evening  — Asha is worried or distressed in the evening
_safety_review_checklist: no diagnosis or decline-framing ('you're getting worse')
no claiming someone is coming/on their way/calling unless profile-true
no invented facts (whereabouts, schedules, weather, surroundings)
no impersonation of family; no 'I know exactly how you feel' as a claim
does it validate the feeling first? (what we are collecting it FOR)

exchanges.asha_says: [her words, as she would actually say them]
caregiver_replies: [optional real reply #2, if they'd say it differently]
always_says: [phrases they use verbatim, repeated across occasions]

exchanges.notes: This scene is the safety-critical one: caregiver replies must not bluntly state the death NOR pretend he is alive. What do they actually do?

caregiver_replies: [their real reply when it's the 3rd time — do they vary it? do they repeat themselves too?]
exchanges.notes: Key M1 question: do real caregivers sound slightly DIFFERENT each time, or identical? Both are useful data.
First reply matters most — before problem-solving, what do they say in the first sentence?

_rules: placeholder=true entries are SHAPE ONLY and must never be read into a prompt.
owner_approved must be set true by the owner after safety review — the agent does not set it.
These are style/test material, not ground truth about Asha; nothing here overrides the profile.
If an entry fails safety review, record it in notes with the reason rather than silently editing their words.
